replacements.after: 1.4 In one chosen Fredholm normal form the projection to perturbation data is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,g(x,y))$, with $x$ in a Banach space and $y$ in a finite-dimensional kernel coordinate space. Criticality is failure of $D_yg$ to surject onto the finite-dimensional second target factor. Shrink the chart and take a closed product $B\times Q$ contained in its domain, where $B$ is a closed Banach ball and $Q$ is a closed finite-dimensional cube. Its critical-value image is closed relative to the target chart: if $(x_j,g(x_j,y_j))$ converges to $(x,z)$, then $x_j\to x$ because $x_j$ is the FIRST TARGET COORDINATE; no compactness of the Banach ball is used. Compactness of $Q$ gives a subsequence $y_j\to y$, and closedness of $B$ and continuity give $(x,y)\in B\times Q$, $g(x,y)=z$. The nonsurjective finite-dimensional derivative condition is closed, so the limit is critical. Intersect this image with a closed inner target ball lying in the coordinate chart to obtain an exclusion closed in the whole perturbation space. It has empty interior: any target open product has some fixed first coordinate $x$, and finite-dimensional Sard for $y\mapsto g(x,y)$ supplies a second coordinate outside its critical values. Countable-basis centers and rational radii give countably many such domain products and inner target balls covering every chart point and its image. Their critical-value images are thus only countably many closed nowhere-dense exclusions. Taking the union over the countable class and family list remains countable. [F2, step 1.3, construct]

[F5] Every spherical gluing below is made with a retained product collar $S^2\times(-2\varepsilon,2\varepsilon)$, chosen disjoint from $U$. For closed pieces $A_-$ and $A_+$ on the negative and positive sides, replace them by the relative-open sets $O_-=A_-\cup(S^2\times(-2\varepsilon,\varepsilon))$ and $O_+=A_+\cup(S^2\times(-\varepsilon,2\varepsilon))$ in their union. On the added collar of $O_-$, send its parameter $t\ge0$ to $(1-s)t$; fix $A_-$. The analogous formula on the negative added collar retracts $O_+$ to $A_+$. Their intersection is $S^2\times(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ and retracts to $S^2$ by $t\mapsto(1-s)t$. These homotopies match the identity on the joining sphere and remain valid after deleting $U$, since the collars miss it. Thus [F2] is applied only to these actual open covers, with the same homology groups as the named closed pieces. The collars are the product collars retained in the chosen smooth ball and connected-sum constructions; no collar for an arbitrary wild sphere is asserted.

The analytic framework referenced there is Ozsváth–Szabó, *Holomorphic disks and topological invariants for closed three-manifolds*, §§3.2–3.6 and §8.4: Fredholm sections for totally real product tori, regular perturbations, oriented compactifications and strip/triangle/quadrilateral gluing with its actual admissibility conditions. The sutured application uses zero multiplicity in every cap/boundary region and the actual periodic-domain/area and boundary-barrier checks made below; it is not a use of an S3-knot analytic theorem for incomplete attaching systems. For good admissible surface cuts, Juhász, *Floer homology and surface decompositions*, GT12 (2008), Proposition7.6, printed pp.330–331, identifies the entire outer disk differential via actual conformal lifts of the rigid bigons/rectangles; the retained local determinant-splicing construction below fixes the specified integral orientation transport. Their source Statements do not assert a ZF+Countable-Choice foundation; no such axiom weakening is inferred here.
